makeToolLinks.capability: Generic OBD-II powertrain-code reading for canonical generic P-family DTCs.
makeToolLinks.restriction: Does not establish manufacturer-specific, body, chassis, network, hybrid/EV, or exact-vehicle compatibility.

makeToolLinks.capability: Cooling-system pressure testing through supplied hose and cap adapters.
makeToolLinks.restriction: Owner must confirm an included adapter matches the vehicle before buying.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: Smoke testing for EVAP, vacuum, intake, exhaust and turbo/boost leaks, with a dedicated 0-1 psi EVAP mode.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Only shown when the How-to-Fix explicitly prescribes a smoke test.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: Battery state of health, CCA and internal-resistance analysis.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Not a true resistive battery load tester; load-test wording is an unresolved-tool hold.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: Low-current DC clamp measurement for explicit parasitic-draw procedures.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Not inferred from a parasitic-drain symptom alone.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: AC/DC voltage and current, resistance, continuity, capacitance, frequency and diode tests.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Not a waveform scope and not inferred when the article does not explicitly prescribe a multimeter.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: 0-300 psi compression testing on gasoline engines with 10, 12, 14 and 18 mm adapters.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Requires explicitly proven gasoline-engine context; suppressed for diesel, EV and unknown engine context.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: Mechanical engine/transmission oil-pressure testing with 0-100 psi and 0-400 psi gauges and 13 adapters.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Owner must confirm the correct engine-port adapter and factory pressure specification.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: 0-100 psi fuel-system pressure testing with a relief valve and brass fittings.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Requires proven compatible low-pressure gasoline application; suppressed for diesel, direct-injection high-pressure rail, flex-fuel and unknown engine context.

reusableReviewedTools.capability: Licensed VCDS interface for diagnostic-capable Volkswagen/Audi Group passenger cars, including manufacturer-specific control-module diagnostics.
reusableReviewedTools.restriction: Limited to supported VAG vehicles and VIN count; 1990-1994 applications require separate legacy/adapter review, and hybrid/EV coverage remains fail-closed here.

holds.excerpt: Clean or replace the flame trap service parts and cracked vacuum hoses first, then clean the throttle body and IAC valve, and replace a faulty Bosch AMM or IAC valve if testing confirms failure.
Test the overdrive solenoid and wiring first.
Replace the overdrive relay (located on the firewall near the brake booster) and test the overdrive solenoid.
Remove the door panel, disconnect the window from the old regulator, install the new unit, and test operation before reassembling.
Typical costs are about $150-$400 for diagnosis/fluid service, $300-$800 for solenoid/valve body repair, and $1,800-$3,000 for a complete rebuild.
Diagnose which component has failed using Volvo VIDA diagnostic software.
Understand that EPA range is tested under ideal conditions - expect 200-230 miles in real-world mixed driving.
Clear fault codes after replacement and perform throttle body adaptation using VIDA diagnostic tool.
Always reset the throttle adaptation values after replacement using a Volvo-compatible scanner (VIDA/DiCE).
Typical cost is about $150-$400 for leak diagnosis and sealing, plus $300-$800 for a REM and programming depending on whether a new OEM module or used unit with matching software support is used.
If the vehicle won't start despite a full high-voltage charge, the BDU may need diagnosis.
Diagnose with VIDA to determine if the motor or module has failed.
Ensure the electric parking brake auto-adjustment is functioning properly through a scan tool procedure.
Diagnose using VIDA to determine which component has failed.
If it will not regen, a forced/static regeneration via diagnostic tool may clear it;
Perform the oil-cap/glove test (whistle or running change when the cap is removed indicates abnormal crankcase pressure).
Diagnose whether the fault is the strut/drive units, the pull-down (cinch) motor, or a calibration/limit issue.
Scan for specific NOx/SCR codes (do not rely on the generic AdBlue message).

Replace the failed upstream or downstream NOx sensor or the AdBlue dosing module/valve as indicated, prime/bleed air from the dosing system, use only fresh, uncontaminated DEF, and clear the fault and reset the SCR system with a diagnostic tool to cancel the no-start countdown.
Have the electric parking brake motor retracted during pad replacement using VIDA diagnostic tool.
Clear fault codes and perform supercharger clutch adaptation using VIDA diagnostic tool.
scan for lean-mixture or idle-related faults as supporting evidence.
Diagnose with VIDA/DiCE to identify which corner is leaking.
Perform a center display reset and network reset, then scan for telematics/infotainment faults.
If problems persist, dealers typically reload software, update the TCAM/infotainment modules, or replace a failed communication/display-related module if diagnostics support it.
Dealers typically update hybrid control software first, then test the onboard charger, battery coolant circuits, contactors, and high-voltage battery components.
